articleSummary: Vietnam is experiencing a concerning increase in hand-foot-and-mouth disease (HFMD), with nearly 3,000 infections reported at the National Children's Hospital in the first two months of 2026. This marks a 56% increase compared to the same period in 2025, with hospitalizations doubling. The majority of affected individuals are children under five years old. While HFMD is typically mild, it can lead to serious complications such as encephalitis, meningitis, myocarditis, and acute pulmonary edema, which can be fatal without prompt treatment. Warning signs requiring urgent medical attention include persistent high fever over 39°C, sudden tremors or spasms, and unsteady movements. Parents are advised to maintain good hygiene practices and avoid antibiotics, as re-infections can occur due to varying strains of the virus.

articleHeadline: Dengue in China: Preventive measures urged amid rising mosquito populations
articleSummary: Guangdong Province is experiencing an increase in dengue fever and chikungunya fever transmission risk due to rising temperatures and rainfall, which promote mosquito breeding. Symptoms of mushroom poisoning include vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea, necessitating prompt hospital care. The situation highlights the dual health risks faced by the population, underscoring the need for awareness and preventive actions.

articleHeadline: Melioidosis in India: Rare cases highlight environmental health risks
articleSummary: A recent case of melioidosis in Raigad, Maharashtra, involved a 58-year-old man who returned from Saudi Arabia. After sustaining a minor cut between his toes and being exposed to dust and muddy water, he developed a severe multisystem infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei. Initial symptoms were misleadingly mild, but the condition escalated to severe knee pain, swelling, and low oxygen levels, leading to deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. The patient required emergency surgery and intensive antibiotic treatment, marking this as the fourth reported case in the region over several decades. Health professionals emphasize the rarity and underdiagnosis of melioidosis, raising concerns about environmental health risks associated with soil and dust exposure.

articleHeadline: Foot And Mouth Disease in Vietnam: Preventive measures urged amid increasing cases
articleSummary: Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) cases are escalating in Vietnam, with over 107,000 reported in 2025, marking a 29% increase from the previous year. Ho Chi Minh City has seen a significant uptick in activity, recording 588 cases in week 10 of 2026, a 38.7% rise from the preceding four weeks, and escalating to 837 cases in week 11. By the end of week 11, the city had logged 7,294 cases, a stark contrast to the 1,917 cases reported by the same time in 2025. The disease primarily affects children under five and is caused by Enteroviruses, with peak periods typically occurring from March to May and September to November. To combat the spread, health authorities recommend adhering to the '3 clean principles': eat clean, live clean, and maintain hand hygiene. Additional preventive measures include avoiding shared utensils, regular cleaning of surfaces and toys, frequent handwashing, and keeping infected children at home to prevent further transmission.
